 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.696/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Vatakara (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 17/03/2018.
The sole respondent herein is the 3rd respondent in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 11/06/2015 at about 06:30 a.m., while he was travelling from Thekkedathu Kadavu to Peruvayal in an autorickshaw bearing registration no.KL-56-K-74, car bearing registration no.KL-60- A-6555 driven by the second respondent in a negligent manner 2025:KER:39502 collided with the autorickshaw and thereby he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent owner and the second respondent driver remained ex parte.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement disputing the negligence of the second respondent.
The age, avocation, income etc. of the claim petitioner were disputed.
The amount of compensation claimed was contended to be excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A11 series and Ext
. C1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Ext. B1
was marked on the side of the third respondent.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an 2025:KER:39502 amount of 3,24,000/- together with interest @
9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the Rasheed vs The New India Assurance Co.Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5249434/

According to the learned counsel for the claim petitioner, in the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 2025:KER:39502 Insurance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236, the notional income of a coolie is liable to be fixed at 10,000/- in the year 2015.

sentences.text: This submission is not opposed by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer.
Hence, the notional income of the claim petitioner is fixed at 10,000/- per month.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 95,741/- (total compensation 4,19,741/- that is, 3,24,000/- granted by the Tribunal + 95,741/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization (excluding the period of 530 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurance company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of 2025:KER:39502 the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
